To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the direct population of the ground state in 160Dy is possible, (ii) the direct population is suppressed by about a factor of 2 compared to the total population, (iii) the direct population increases with increasing impact parameter, (iv) the direct population can be enhanced by using a 2n reaction, and (v) the direct population decreases with increasing excitation energy of the projectile.
the probability of cold 2n-transfer to yrast states increases from 7 % at grazing collisions up-to ≈ 50% for large impact parameters.

The population probability of the 160Dy ground state in the reaction 162 D y ( 116 S n, 1 18 S n ) 160 D y increases from 7 % to ≈ 50 % with increasing impact parameter, while the population probability of the spherical 2 n transfer product 1 18 Sn stays at about 45 % for all measured impact parameter.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the reaction dynamics in the region of heavy transfer reactions.
the development of a new method for the study of nuclear structure in the vicinity of a Coulomb barrier using a 2n pickup reaction.

the development and application of a new technique to study the population of intrinsicaly cold states in the compound nucleus in a 2neutron transfer reaction at energies in the proximity of the Coulomb-barrier.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 2n transfer probability is a strong function of the impact parameter, while the 4p-4h transfer probability is a weak function of the impact.
the 2n transfer to 160Dy is dominated by a direct transfer process at grazing impact parameters, and by an inelastic scattering process at large impact parameters.
the direct 2n transfer to intrinsically cold 2n states in 160Dy is possible, but only at small impact parameters, while at large impact parameters the population of yrast states in 160Gd is favored.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cold transfer reactions, in particular for deformed target nuclei, can be used to produce a large variety of nuclei in a very clean way.
the population of the ground state in 118Sn in a 2p-4h transfer reaction is not affected by the deformation of the target and projectile nuclei.
we can select the cold 2n-transfer process in 162D y(116Sn, 118Sn)160 Dy at large impact parameters.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it should be feasible to select cold 2n-transfer reactions for the synthesis of super heavy nuclei.

the population of cold yrast states in 160Dy is enhanced by a factor ≈ 2 compared to the population of the spherical ground state in 118Sn, which is in agreement with the results obtained in the 162Dy + 124Sn reaction at 6 MeV/u [1].
cold reactions can be selected by suppressing excitations to high spin states in the deforming product nucleus.
